questions.text: Which three pieces are required for a basic Three.js render setup?
questions.explanation: A minimal Three.js application needs a scene, a camera, and a renderer.

questions.text: What does geometry represent in a mesh?
questions.explanation: Geometry defines the structure or shape of the object, while material controls appearance.

questions.text: Why is `requestAnimationFrame` commonly used in Three.js apps?
options: To compile shaders on the server
questions.explanation: `requestAnimationFrame` drives the browser-friendly render loop used for animations and interaction.

questions.text: Which loader is commonly used for modern 3D models in Three.js?
questions.explanation: GLTFLoader is widely used for importing glTF and GLB models into Three.js scenes.

questions.text: What is raycasting used for in a 3D scene?
options: Detecting intersections for selection or hover
questions.explanation: Raycasting is the usual way to detect which objects a pointer intersects in 3D space.

questions.text: Why should shadows be enabled selectively?
questions.explanation: Shadows improve realism but can significantly increase rendering work.

questions.text: What should happen when the viewport size changes?
options: Update camera aspect and renderer size
Delete the scene and rebuild it
questions.explanation: Resize handling usually updates the camera projection and renderer dimensions.

questions.text: Which practice helps avoid memory leaks in Three.js apps?
options: Cleaning up controls, listeners, and WebGL resources
questions.explanation: Cleanup matters because WebGL resources and listeners can survive longer than intended.

questions.text: What is a mesh in Three.js?
questions.explanation: A mesh is the combination of shape data and appearance data that can be rendered in the scene.

questions.text: Why is measuring performance important before optimizing a Three.js scene?
options: It shows where frame time is actually being spent
questions.explanation: Profiling reveals whether bottlenecks come from draw calls, shaders, assets, CPU work, or something else.

questions.text: Explain the difference between geometry, material, and mesh in Three.js.
questions.explanation: Geometry describes shape, material describes visual appearance, and a mesh combines both into a renderable object.

questions.text: Why should asset loading be treated as asynchronous application state?
questions.explanation: Models and textures can fail or arrive late, so apps need loading, success, and error states instead of assuming immediate availability.

questions.text: What are the most common causes of poor Three.js performance?
questions.explanation: Heavy geometry, large textures, too many draw calls, expensive shadows, and excessive work inside the animation loop are common causes.

questions.text: Describe how raycasting can be used to implement object selection.
questions.explanation: Convert pointer position into normalized coordinates, cast a ray from the camera into the scene, and inspect which selectable objects the ray intersects.

questions.text: What cleanup work is important when unmounting a Three.js view inside a web app?
questions.explanation: Remove listeners, stop animation loops if needed, dispose geometries, materials, and textures, and tear down controls or scene-related helpers.
